s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with bleeding after trauma, and concurrent lipolymphedema and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Patient had an intracranial hemorrhage
Patient had recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs is attributed to functional venous insufficiency
Patient has been wearing compression stockings for years
Family history of similar conditions
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

per_call: Congenital lipomatous overgrowth with vascular, epidermal, and skeletal anomalies

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, which is associated with cerebral cavernous malformations

shortlist.label: Familial cerebral cavernous malformations
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and patient's father died of an intracranial hemorrhage, suggesting a hereditary component

shortlist.label: Venous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations, consistent with venous malformations

shortlist.label: Cutaneous venous malformations
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, consistent with cutaneous venous malformations

shortlist.label: Glomuvenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis, partly showing thrombosis, which is consistent with glomuvenous malformations

raw.rationale: The patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage, right-sided hemiparesis, and hemianopsia, combined with the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, strongly supports this diagnosis. KRIT1 mutations are commonly associated with Cerebral Cavernous Malformations.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has vascular malformations and lipolymphedema, the presence of a KRIT1 variant and the specific neurological symptoms point more towards Cerebral Cavernous Malformations.

rejected.label: Parkes Weber Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically involves a capillary malformation, arteriovenous malformation, and/or a lymphatic malformation, but the genetic findings and neurological history in this case are more indicative of Cerebral Cavernous Malformations.

rejected.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations, but the specific KRIT1 variant and the patient's neurological symptoms are more consistent with Cerebral Cavernous Malformations.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves a port-wine stain and neurological symptoms, but the patient's presentation and genetic findings do not align with the typical characteristics of Sturge-Weber Syndrome.
